arguments.distinguishes: The sampled plan records separate the competing explanations directly: optimization_raw_status and optimization_selected_iteration show whether solves end by requested stop (compute budget) rather than convergence, effective_horizon shows whether the terminal/holding horizon is truncated relative to the configured 10, and actual_tension_n shows whether per-channel loading approaches the 8.0 N limit. A late-run pattern of User_Requested_Stop with truncated effective_horizon would retain the compute-budget/solver-termination explanations while leaving the tip-speed-penalty explanation as the residual, whereas a converged full-horizon solve with tensions inside the limit would point to cost design rather than compute budget — a distinction not obtainable from the sampled summary alone.

expected.observation: Sampled updates report optimization_raw_status = User_Requested_Stop with update_wall_s far above the 0.01 s control period.
Sampled updates predominantly report Solve_Succeeded with effective_horizon = 10 inside the control period.
Sampled updates terminate by User_Requested_Stop or Maximum_Iterations_Exceeded with optimization_selected_iteration below max_iterations 120.
Sampled updates report Solve_Succeeded with optimization_selected_iteration reaching convergence.
Sampled actual_tension_n stays at or below the 8.0 N per-tendon limit.
Sampled actual_tension_n reaches or exceeds the 8.0 N per-tendon limit.
Sampled plan records show accepted plans with the raised holding_tip_speed_weight present but expose no per-term cost contributions.

limitations: The plans query samples at most 8 of 35 update records; unqueried updates remain not_read.
optimization_raw_status, optimization_selected_iteration and effective_horizon are controller-side plan records, not backend motion, and are not causal evidence.
A requested-stop status string does not by itself establish that plan quality caused the sampled holding failure.
One execution and one paired comparison cannot establish a dominant cause; no closed-loop counterfactual replay is available.
Frames are kept distinct: world for tip vectors, projected GVS coordinates for state, serial backend joint coordinates for q/qdot.
missing_information: Per-update optimization_raw_status and optimization_selected_iteration for all 35 controller updates; only a sampled subset is inspectable per query.
Per-update effective_horizon across the run, to test whether the terminal/holding horizon is truncated relative to the configured horizon 10.
Per-update per-channel actual_tension_n across the run to assess proximity to the 8.0 N per-tendon limit.
Sampled backend motion over the full trajectory t=0.01-0.35 s; only the final 0.05 s holding window is currently supplied.
Full historical warm plans and optimizer iteration traces are not retained (control_snapshots.json absent).
arguments.question: Do the retained per-update plan records show systematic budget-driven early solver termination and/or a truncated effective_horizon across the run (especially the final holding window), and do per-channel applied tensions stay within the 8.0 N limit — thereby distinguishing a compute-budget/solver-termination limitation from the insufficient hold tip-speed penalty as the explanation for the sampled holding-speed failure?

relationships.relevance: Both runs record deadline_misses 35 of 35 updates (F90 baseline, F29 candidate) at control_period_s 0.01 s (F274, F76) with mean complete-update time 17.26331904856488 s (F49) and 17.77877309145406 s (F114), and the recorded stopping count is dominated by User_Requested_Stop 34 (F515) under max_iterations 120 (F525); this concerns the named budget-saturation hypothesis because it is consistent with plan selection being cut by the compute budget.

Recorded solver stopping counts are User_Requested_Stop 34 (F515), Solve_Succeeded 1 (F457) and Maximum_Iterations_Exceeded 1 (F541) under a configured max_iterations of 120 (F525) and horizon 10 (F537), so the named termination-limitation hypothesis cannot be separated from cost design without the per-update raw status.

force_bound_violation_n is 0.0 in both runs (F134 baseline, F343 candidate), which is evidence against an actuator-limit violation driving the held speed at run level; it is only partial because per-channel applied tensions remain unread.

The holding tip-speed weight is 0.0 in the baseline recipe (F462) and 0.05 in the candidate recipe (F538), yet the candidate sampled holding speed is 1.1750052670100422 m/s (F160, F471) against the 0.02 m/s limit (F440), about 59x, so an insufficient hold tip-speed penalty remains consistent with the residual holding-speed failure.

stopping_conditions: Stop after the single plans-view query returns the sampled per-update records or reports the entry unavailable.
Stop when the sampled records establish whether raw solver status and effective_horizon are systematic and whether sampled tensions stay within the 8.0 N limit, or when coverage is reported missing.
Stop within wall_s 180 and one tool call; no numerical check, backend solve, or production change.
